headline: Bayern confirm Kane deal; rumours stir for Madrid, City, Arsenal
paragraphs: The one confirmed piece of business today is Bayern Munich's extension of Harry Kane's contract, per Transfermarkt, which had been due to expire this summer; the report notes no pay rise despite Kane's Ballon d'Or win. Everything else below remains speculative. No item in today's feed was independently corroborated by more than one newsroom: the handful of 'also' tags present are BBC Sport repeating BBC Gossip, or Sky Sports repeating Sky Transfers, the same outlet twice, not separate confirmation.

On the rumour side, Transfermarkt reports Arsenal are tracking winger Antonio Nusa while Liverpool are watching an unnamed Fenerbahce player. Separately, Transfermarkt says Real Madrid are expected to sign Manchester United academy prospect JJ Gabriel in January, and FourFourTwo reports Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain are both circling a new Aston Villa signing. None of this is confirmed by any club involved, and it should be read as speculation rather than fact.

Away from the market, FourFourTwo's analysis says Manchester City are 'unlikely' to be stripped of past titles but could face further Premier League charges, the outlet's own assessment rather than a league finding. On the pitch, Sky Sports notes Liverpool failed to register a shot on target at home for the first time in 442 Premier League games, in their match against Arsenal; Iraola has since said Liverpool must sacrifice control for creativity ahead of this weekend's trip to Crystal Palace.
